title: The Assassination of the Duke of Guise
source: Musée Condé, Chantilly (public domain). Wikimedia Commons: Paul Delaroche - L'assassinat du duc de Guise au chateau de Blois en 1588 - Google Art Project.jpg (4207 x 2408 px). Verify the file description says Musée Condé (the 1834 oil), not a replica or the 1832 watercolour.
caption: A duke lies dead. Who gave the order? #truecrime #frenchhistory #delaroche #renaissance #storytime
_verify: VERIFIED, Wikipedia EN (The Assassination of the Duke of Guise (Delaroche)): 1834, 57 x 98 cm, Musée Condé; assassination of Henry I, Duke of Guise, by Henry III's guard (the Forty-Five) on 23 December 1588 at Blois; Henry III appears from behind a curtain to see the body. Victorian Web: murder in the king's own bedroom at Blois; Delaroche presents Guise as a sort of Christian martyr.
GENERAL HISTORY (low risk): Guise led the Catholic League and was hugely popular; summoned early in the morning and stabbed; Henry III was himself assassinated in August 1589.
CAUTIOUS: 'taller dead than alive' is a traditional anecdote, phrased as legend on slide 7.
Small figures: zoom boxes must stay readable; if the king is tiny, widen slide 6-7 boxes.
Focus boxes estimated without seeing the image; re-tune on the real image and fix any text that names a detail that is not visible.

slides.headline: A duke lies dead. Who gave the order?
slides.sub: Paul Delaroche, The Assassination of the Duke of Guise, 1834

slides.headline: Blois, 1588
slides.text: Château de Blois, 23 December 1588. France is torn apart by religious war, and one man is more popular than the king himself.

slides.headline: The duke
slides.text: Henry, Duke of Guise, leader of the Catholic League, lies dead on the floor. A few minutes ago he was the most feared man in France.

slides.headline: The killers
slides.text: Across the room, his killers wait, still holding their weapons. They are the king's own bodyguards, the Forty-Five.

slides.headline: The bedroom
slides.text: And this is the king's own bedroom. The duke was summoned early in the morning and stabbed as he came in.

slides.headline: The king
slides.text: Now look at the curtain. Stepping out from behind it: King Henry III himself. He ordered the murder, and now he comes to look.

slides.headline: Taller dead
slides.text: Legend says the king stared at the body and said the duke looked even taller dead than alive.

slides.headline: A martyr?
slides.text: Yet Delaroche lays the duke out almost like a Christian martyr. The killer is a king, and the victim looks like a saint.

slides.headline: What came next
slides.text: The murder did not end the war. Months later, Henry III was stabbed to death himself. Who was the real villain here?
